1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and Sri Ajit Kumar Singh holding brief of Sri Anil Kumar Tiwari, learned Counsel for the complainant and perused the record.
Despite service of notice, no one appeared on behalf of the complainant.
2. The applicant seeks enlargement on bail in FIR No.170 of 2023, under Sections 363, 366, 376 IPC and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act, Police Station Gosaiganj, District Ayodhya.
3. The FIR in question was lodged as a missing person report.

Subsequently, in the statements under Sections 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C., the victim did not support the prosecution story and stated Akhandmani Chaudhary Dhom vs State Of U.P. Thru. Its Prin. Secy. ... on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130460295/
1 that she had gone out of her own freewill and had married in a Arya Samaj Mandir.

sentences.text: The victim had refused to undergo the medical examination.
There is no definite material with regard to the age of the victim as provided under the Juvenile Justice Act and the Rules framed thereunder.
No report of the test as directed in the order dated 20.12.2023 is on record.
The applicant is in custody since 03.09.2023.
4. Learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the bail prayer.

5. Considering the statements under Sections 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C. which do not support the prosecution story, the refusal of the victim to undergo medical test and there being no definite material with regard to the age of the victim coupled with the fact that the applicant is in custody since 03.09.2023 and has no criminal antecedents, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

6. Let the applicant Akhandmani Chaudhary Dhom be released on bail in the aforesaid first information report on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
